nodes.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide.* Examples: If 6 × 4 = 24 is known, then 4 × 6 = 24 is also known. set.reason: Factor-order manipulation and comparison of laws help notation. An array split directly establishes distribution without the three-factor regrouping procedure.
set.scope: rewriting forms of the distributive law

set.reason: This algebraic route uses the perfect-square identity before verifying the decimal digit coefficients. A finite geometric-sum encoding and a perfect-square expansion form one algebraic digit-proof route. Direct place-value/column carry arguments can avoid those particular formulas.
set.scope: Expand the square of 10^k-1 in the observed repeated-eights and repeated-fives product.

set.reason: The observed proof needs finite sums of powers of ten; a direct column-carry proof would be an alternative. A finite geometric-sum encoding and a perfect-square expansion form one algebraic digit-proof route. Direct place-value/column carry arguments can avoid those particular formulas.
set.scope: Encode repeated digits and verify the resulting long digit identity by finite geometric sums.

criteria: Express each repeated-digit integer exactly and derive the product in powers of ten.
Verify all decimal coefficients are valid digits after carries or borrowing, including endpoints, before summing or locating digits.
set.description: Encode repeated decimal digits as finite geometric sums and determine exact product digits using place-value identities and justified carries or borrowing. Prove a proposed long digit pattern before taking its digit sum.
set.name: Exact decimal digits of repdigit products
